rows.consequence: A scientifically independent calibration artifact is mapped to unavailable/not-resolvable by the default CLI. Conversely, following the only passing default example derives the detection threshold from the claim-outcome bundles it gates, destroying oracle independence and making floor clearance outcome-dependent. This is both a claim-validity defect and failure of the canonical reproducible campaign-to-claim flow.
rows.counterevidence: The independent-floor failure is conservative, and P2-039 artifacts are structurally and arithmetically validated. A typed FloorRequest resolver exists and can perform exact or conservative transported resolution, but it is reachable from analyze_claims only through the private test seam. The same-bundle integration fixture is synthetic and does not itself publish a claim.
evidence_refs: Bounded absence search: git grep -n -E '_floor_request_factory|FloorRequest\(' BASE_HEAD -- '*.py' found the private engine parameter, one private integration injection, and unit-test constructors, but no production/CLI FloorRequest factory.
rows.finding: The canonical public claim path cannot consume an independently calibrated exact or transported P2-039 floor: analyze_claims exposes only a private request-factory seam defaulting to None, while its fallback exact resolver accepts a cell only when every consumer claim bundle/config pair is also present among that floor cell's calibration bundle observations. The integration oracle makes this circular condition pass by rewriting floor observations to the claim bundles themselves.

rows.consequence: A J/output-token contrast can satisfy stop_reason_required even when no realized stop reason was ingested. rows.consequence: A one-item or one-token boundary change can enable or block the entire scored campaign and its eventual AP-5 claims, but reviewers cannot tell whether the verdict is robust to nearby defensible thresholds or why these cutoffs represent a valid envelope rather than an arbitrary policy choice.
rows.counterevidence: The constants are frozen in code, emitted in the verdict artifact, deterministic, and mostly conservative; E1 explicitly reports that 5% means zero tolerance at n=8. E5's n=10 threshold is advisory and does not gate. The finding does not assert that a current verdict is wrong, only that the future claim prerequisite lacks an auditable threshold rationale/sensitivity record in the authorized evidence set.

rows.finding: The AP-5 prerequisite envelope verdict is controlled by un-rationalized point thresholds with no sensitivity result in the supplied authority/oracle set: exactly eight items per level; E1 non-EOS rate and spread <=0.05, which degenerates to zero tolerated non-EOS items at n=8; E2 mean spread <=1 token; E3 permutation p>=0.01 with 10000 draws; and E4 prompt range/mean spread <=4/2 tokens. Any one flips the overall validated/failed verdict.
